environment: Local isolated PostgreSQL database with a simple approval workflow and a connected requester LiveView
method: QueryProbe all-process capture of one transition-reason change after settling the LiveView mailbox. Baseline restores the parent UserAuth and Tenant read paths; candidate uses the same fixture with navigation reuse. The additive migration is present in both runs. Only aggregate counters are retained.
correctness: Every protected callback still validates the current session, user, organization, membership and grants.
Fresh access fingerprints and catalog generations invalidate presentation data even when broadcasts are missed.
Publication label and role-binding changes update both connected tabs on their next protected event.
Session expiry and membership revocation redirect even when navigation would otherwise be reused.
The generation changes atomically with publication; uncommitted and rolled-back publications are invisible to readers.
Runtime generation access is tenant scoped and read-only; the trigger function uses a fixed search path and has no public EXECUTE grant.
Populated forward migrations backfill counters; backup/restore retains the counters and application data.
deployment: Apply the additive migration before new code. Its publication-table lock protects backfill and trigger installation. Keep the additive schema when rolling back application code.
limitations: The generation lookup adds a small indexed subquery to each scoped organization read, without adding a round trip.
Counters serialize publication changes within a tenant; normal reads do not lock the counter row.
The cache contains at most 25 navigation entries and is presentation data, never command authority.
Local SQL counts are not a hosted latency or capacity claim; full deferred-cycle and connection-occupancy measurements remain pending.
